solution.text:
1. Oscillating rope
A. Physical pendulum model
The first mode has little curvature, so approximate the rope by a uniform rigid rod pivoted at its upper end. For rope mass \(M\), its moment of inertia and centre-of-mass distance from the pivot are \(I=ML^2/3\) and \(b=L/2\). Small-angle torque gives \(I\ddot\theta=-Mgb\theta\). Thus
\[f_1\simeq\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{Mgb}{I}}=\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{3g}{2L}}\simeq0.61\,\mathrm{Hz},\qquad T_1\simeq1.6\,\mathrm s.\]
This is a model estimate, not the exact flexible-rope eigenfrequency. Explain the model in the reasoning field.
B. Similarity below a node
Dimensional analysis gives \(f_k(L)=c_k\sqrt{g/L}\), where \(c_k\) depends only on the mode number. A node is stationary, so the rope below it behaves as a shorter hanging rope. Let \(A\) be the suspension point, \(B\) the free end, and \(N\) the second-mode node.

\[f_2(L)=f_1(L-NA),\qquad \frac{f_2(L)}{f_1(L)}=\sqrt{\frac{L}{L-NA}}\simeq\sqrt{\frac1{0.2}}\simeq2.2.\]
The part below the upper third-mode node \(N_1\) is in its second mode, and \(L-N_1A\simeq0.4L\). Therefore
\[f_3(L)=f_2(L-N_1A),\quad \frac{f_3}{f_2}\simeq\sqrt{\frac1{0.4}}\simeq1.6,\quad \frac{f_3}{f_1}\simeq2.2\times1.6\simeq3.5.\]
\[f_1:f_2:f_3\simeq1:2.2:3.5.\]
The source has minor index and length-label typos in this argument. The relations above explicitly use the length below each node. The original marking tables remain in the reference PDF.
